narrative.overview:
The whole body of work is one instrument. A dark obsidian ground carries brass that looks engraved, not lit: hairline rules, double rims, inscribed numerals, a degree limb. Projects are pointers on the rotating rete, placed on rings by their real maturity. Work that is still growing is marked in verdigris, the patina brass picks up over time. Text is parchment, warm and quiet, so the instrument and the work lead and the chrome stays back.

Density is calm. Panels are few and framed like plates set into the instrument. Most structure comes from engraved hairlines, inventory numbers (`AH·01`) and a single ledger, not from stacked cards. Motion is slow and damped, like a heavy rete turning on a pin. Nothing bounces, nothing glows.

This world replaces an earlier dark-glass/aurora look. It refuses frosted glass, neon gradients, gradient text and glow halos. Legacy class names (`.glass`, `.text-gradient`) survive only so older routes inherit the new engraved treatment.
keyCharacteristics: Obsidian ground with one warm radial brass wash at the top of the page.
Brass is the only accent of the shell; verdigris appears only to mean "still growing".
Engraved hairlines and double rules everywhere a border or divider is needed.
Marcellus inscriptions for display and scale labels; Alegreya Sans for reading.
Maturity is always shown honestly as the astrolabe's Roman ring numerals I–IV, on the instrument and in every status badge.
Each project keeps its own accent theme, but it shows only inside that project's own scope (its detail page, its ledger row's hover). The shared shell and home cards stay brass.

rules.name: The Patina Rule
rules.body: Verdigris means "still growing" and nothing else. Mature work is brass; early work is verdigris. Never use verdigris as decoration.

rules.name: The One Metal Rule
rules.body: The shell has one accent, brass. Other hues enter only through a project's own theme, inside that project's own scope. Cards that list many projects stay brass.

rules.name: The Legible Ink Rule
rules.body: Readable text uses parchment, parchment-soft, parchment-muted, brass or brass-bright. brass-deep and verdigris-dim are fills, not ink.

rules.name: The Single Weight Rule
rules.body: Marcellus ships one weight (400). Headings never get a bold, and `font-synthesis: none` stays on so the browser can't fake one. Emphasis in display text comes from colour (brass-bright), not weight.

rules.name: The Figures Rule
rules.body: Running text uses old-style figures; tables and stats (`.tabular`) switch to tabular lining figures.

rules.name: The Inscription Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked Marcellus is for inscriptions: numbers, scale labels and field labels inside a panel. It never sits above a section heading as a kicker.

rules.name: The Engraved Not Lit Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from double rims and dark drop shadows. Brass never glows: no coloured box-shadows, no halos, no backdrop blur.

dos: **Do** keep the shell to brass on obsidian, and let a project's own theme colour only its own scope.
**Do** show maturity honestly with the I–IV ring numerals, the same on the instrument and in badges; mature work goes nearest the centre.
**Do** lay out lists of projects or facts as engraved ledger rows before reaching for cards.
**Do** draw borders and dividers as brass hairlines (14% / 30%), and use the 3px double rule for section breaks.
**Do** use the world easing `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` with slow durations (300–700ms, 1s for entrances), and respect reduced motion.
**Do** set headings in Marcellus 400 and give them emphasis with brass-bright, not weight.
**Do** keep readable text at parchment-muted (4.9:1) or brighter.
donts: **Don't** use frosted glass, backdrop blur, gradient text, neon or aurora gradients, or glow halos. This world replaced that look.
**Don't** use verdigris for anything other than growing or early work.
**Don't** tint shared surfaces (home and series cards, hero pills) with a project's theme hue; that hue belongs on the project's own page.
**Don't** fake a bold Marcellus or put a tracked uppercase kicker above a section heading.
**Don't** make bouncy or springy-overshoot motion. The instrument turns heavily and settles.
**Don't** replace the ledger or astrolabe with a card-grid hero.
**Don't** set small text in brass-deep or verdigris-dim.
